problems.title: A line chart of steps in a week
problems.prompt:
Draw a line chart of daily steps over one week. Put `days` on the x-axis and `steps` on the y-axis, and mark each value with a circle marker (`marker="o"`).
Set the title to `Steps this week`, the x-axis label to `Day`, and the y-axis label to `Steps`.
hints: `ax.plot()` takes the x values first and the y values next. Set the marker with the `marker=` argument.
Add the title with `set_title()` and the axis labels with `set_xlabel()` and `set_ylabel()`.
problems.explain:
`fig, ax = plt.subplots()` makes a place to draw, and `ax.plot(days, steps, marker="o")` connects the steps for each day with a line. With `marker="o"`, a circle marks each day, so it is easy to read which value belongs to which day. Then `set_title()`, `set_xlabel()`, and `set_ylabel()` add the title and the axis labels.
If you swap the two values, as in `ax.plot(steps, days)`, the days move to the y-axis and the trend over the week is hard to read. If you leave out the x values, as in `ax.plot(steps)`, the x-axis shows position numbers starting at 0 instead of days. Grading redraws the chart with different steps and days, so typing the values straight into a list will not pass.
problems.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

days = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
steps = [6800, 9200, 7500, 10400, 8100, 13200, 4600]

# Write your code here
problems.solution:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

days = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
steps = [6800, 9200, 7500, 10400, 8100, 13200, 4600]

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(days, steps, marker="o")
ax.set_title("Steps this week")
ax.set_xlabel("Day")
ax.set_ylabel("Steps")
plt.show()
